title: Felix and the Trail
premise: Sebastian Amberdale, a mountain guide blacklisted from Nepal and Peru after a disaster he refuses to explain, has spent ten years leading low-stakes river runs in Southeast Asia, measuring life in miles. When his old rival Marguerite Voss hires his crew for a salvage job up the Nam Kha, they discover the cargo is the lost expedition ledger of the man who died on Sebastian's last climb — and the permits that let them travel expire with the monsoon's first flood. Betrayed midriver by a crew member selling their route, Sebastian must choose between salvaging the ledger and saving the stranger who helped them, a village ferrywoman named Lin whose own memory of the dead climber forces him to finally claim his identity. They lose the boat but reach the concession post as the waters rise, delivering the ledger to the climber's daughter; Sebastian signs his real name for the first time in a decade, ending the book not with redemption granted but with truth told.
about_author: Casper Joubert is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on the Mekong tributaries before turning to writing full-time. He lives in a converted boathouse and claims he still checks the water level every morning out of habit.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He leads a routine tourist run down the Salween, counting rapids instead of birthdays, and we see how carefully he avoids maps of anywhere he once loved. A letter arrives offering work he can't refuse. Emotional beat: restless avoidance masking grief.

chapters.title: The Rival's Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marguerite Voss appears at his dock with a contract: salvage a sealed crate from an upstream wreck before concession permits lapse. She knows about the blacklist; she implies she knows why. Emotional beat: old resentment sharpened into wary curiosity.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter from deckhand Tomas's POV. The crew assembles — engineer Priya, diver Okonkwo, and quiet cook Anselm — each carrying a reason to say yes to bad money. Tomas senses Sebastian is hiding something about the destination. Emotional beat: fragile camaraderie forming over shared desperation.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The old boat Meridian fights the current through narrowing gorges. Priya patches a hull seam and notices the engine logs have been altered — someone aboard is lying about the route. Emotional beat: competence and creeping suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ferrywoman
chapters.summary: Lin's POV, first appearance. At a flooded crossing village, Lin agrees to pilot them through a channel no outsider knows, asking nothing but passage for her own cargo. She watches Sebastian too closely. Emotional beat: guarded recognition between two people who share a ghost.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn the Nam Kha is the river below the mountain where client Elias Thorne died ten years ago — the climb that got Sebastian blacklisted. Marguerite knew all along. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Radio reports confirm the flood front will arrive days early. The crew votes: push on or turn back. Sebastian chooses forward; Tomas quietly radios coordinates to someone. Emotional beat: commitment hardening while trust begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hold
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The patched seam fails overnight; the hold floods and soaks half their supplies. Lin teaches them her trick of riding shallow channels, earning grudging respect. Emotional beat: humility learned through shared labor.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They open the crate early: it holds Thorne's expedition ledger, pages in his handwriting, including notes suggesting the fatal climb was sabotaged — and that Sebastian was blamed for another's choice. Emotional beat: the past reordering itself.

chapters.title: Anselm's Silence
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. The cook is revealed as Thorne's former expedition doctor, carrying guilt of his own; he confirms the sabotage but not who did it. Tomas grows more nervous. Emotional beat: confession as both wound and relief.

chapters.title: Concession Line
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV via radio transcript and scene at the permit post downstream. Officials warn the permits void at first flood; Marguerite pressures the crew by radio to hurry, revealing she wants the ledger's pages about mineral rights, not memory. Emotional beat: ambition unmasked.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Lin's POV. They shelter in her home village, where elders recognize Thorne's name — he stayed there before the climb, and Lin was a child he taught to read maps. She shows Sebastian his own younger face in an old photograph. Emotional beat: belonging offered where he least expects it.

chapters.title: Tomas's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His debtors surface at the village landing; his betrayal exposed, he confesses he sold the route to Marguerite's backers, who want the ledger destroyed to bury the sabotage evidence. Emotional beat: shame met, unexpectedly, with mercy.

chapters.title: First Flood
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Sebastian's POV. The monsoon hits early. The Meridian tears loose, and the crew saves the crate but loses the boat and most of their gear, stranding them forty miles from the concession post with permits expiring in three days. Emotional beat: loss stripping everything to essentials.

chapters.title: Lin's Channel
chapters.summary: Lin's POV. She offers her late father's ferry barge — barely seaworthy — if Sebastian will carry her cargo: Thorne's letters to the village, which she never delivered. Emotional beat: two cargoes becoming one purpose.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Nameless
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The barge run through the worst gorge, near-drowning, Okonkwo diving to free a fouled rudder. Tomas redeems himself at the rope lines. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: Marguerite Arrives
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marguerite's launch intercepts them; she offers Sebastian reinstatement, his licenses restored, if he hands over the pages naming the saboteur — her late partner. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare, and refused.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Daughter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her motive cracks open: the saboteur was her father, and she wanted the evidence burned to protect his name. Sebastian offers her something harder than destruction — the truth, witnessed. Emotional beat: grief recognizing grief.

chapters.title: Last Miles
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Against the rising water they make the final stretch, barge failing, crew poling through drowned forest as the permit clock runs out. Emotional beat: exhaustion transformed into collective will.

chapters.title: The Concession Post
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They arrive as officials wade to meet them, crate intact, minutes before the flood closes the channel. Sebastian delivers the ledger to Thorne's daughter waiting there — and tells the whole story aloud, on record, for the first time. Emotional beat: truth spoken without flinching.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Lin's POV. Aftermath: Marguerite withdraws her claim and funds the village school; Tomas stays to rebuild the ferry route. Lin asks Sebastian what name he'll use now. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, debts honored.

chapters.title: Felix and the Trail
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, coda. We learn 'Felix' was Thorne's nickname for him — the lucky one who lived. Sebastian signs his real name on the new guide registry, takes Lin's hand, and stops counting miles. Emotional beat: identity claimed, belonging chosen.
